row: Named after its founder, Marita Baquiran Yasuda, this homegrown sanctuary first started in earnest back in 2007, right in Yasuda’s own backyard in Antipolo, Rizal, Philippines. What started out as an effort to rehabilitate one injured stray soon grew into a full-blown sanctuary; one that rarely (if ever) turns away the many abandoned, abused, and neglected stray cats and dogs that turn up on their doorstep. Having since relocated to a more sizeable lot in Morong, Rizal, the shelter now counts over 1400 feline and canine residents under its care. Of course, along with the ever increasing number of animals is a seemingly endless stream of veterinary and utility bills—one day’s worth of food alone can cost upwards of P25,000 (approximately USD500).
